ev.q: During 2020, 88.7% of children and adolescents aged 6–17 years had roads, sidewalks, paths, or trails
Availability of these spaces was less common among children and adolescents who lived in families with incomes <200% of FPL (85.6%)
was consistent among children and adolescents in both urban (89.4% versus 93.9%) and rural (64.9% versus 77.4%) areas.
Regardless of income, availability of spaces to walk or ride a bicycle was lower among children and adolescents living in rural areas
Estimates are based on household interviews of a sample of the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population.
